_comment: The browser-3d platform (DESIGN 1, platform 2): one HTML file, a three.js scene
drawn by a generic shell. A definition that declares this platform must declare
these types exactly and offer these five functions; $State is the record type
start returns, the same throughout. step is called every animation frame with
what the player is pressing; act on a click ("click") or a HUD button.
brief: how the shell calls the app, for whoever decides what to make; examples: how to pin it, for the tester.
name: browser-3d
conventions: Units are metres and radians, except fov: the vertical field of view in degrees (e.g. 70).
y is up. The camera looks along -z when yaw is 0; yaw turns left (counter-clockwise seen
from above) as it grows; pitch looks up as it grows. Facing yaw, forward is
A box/plane/cylinder's size is its full width (x), height (y) and depth (z); a sphere's
diameter is size.x. A plane lies flat (in x-z) at position.y. rotation_y turns an object
about its vertical axis. color is "#rrggbb".
keys are KeyboardEvent.key in lower case ("w", "a", "s", "d", " ", "shift",
"arrowup" ...). mouse_dx/mouse_dy are pixels moved since the last frame, and are 0 unless
brief: start is called when the app opens, with what was saved last time (or null).
step is called every animation frame (about 60 times a second) with `input`: the keys held now, the mouse movement since the last frame, and whether the pointer is locked.
Movement must not depend on the frame rate: keep the time of the last step in the state and move by speed x (now - last), where now - last is the time since the previous step (0 on the first).
Mouse look turns yaw by -mouse_dx x sensitivity and pitch by -mouse_dy x sensitivity, pitch kept within [-1.5, 1.5].
act(state, "click", now) is called on a click on the scene (the click also locks the pointer); HUD buttons call act with their action. If act throws, the shell keeps the old state.

screen is called every frame and returns a Scene: the camera, the objects, and the HUD -- a list of nodes (heading, text, button with its action and whether it is enabled; non-button nodes have action "" and enabled true) drawn over the scene, top left.
Objects are boxes, spheres, planes and cylinders, each a single colour; light, shadow and sky are the shell's. That is the whole vocabulary.
save is called once a second and after every act.
examples: Pin the scene where an item is about it: examples of screen, and of step with inputs, for a few states, judged by `matches` or `holds` on the objects and nodes the item is about -- not every one of them.
Where a number is compared (equals, matches), keep it exact: pick speeds, times and positions whose results are exact in binary (halves, quarters), and keep yaw 0 in examples that move.
